      "text": "Based on the image provided, the step shown is the application of the **derivative** using the **Chain Rule**.\n\nHere is the step-by-step breakdown of how the first line transforms into the second line.\n\n### Core Mathematical Rules Used\n1.  **Derivative of a Constant:** The derivative of $+C$, $+C_1$, or $+C_2$ is **0**, so they disappear in the second step.\n2.  **Derivative of Natural Log (Chain Rule):**\n    $$ \\frac{d}{dx} \\ln(u) \u003d \\frac{1}{u} \\cdot u\u0027 \u003d \\frac{u\u0027}{u} $$\n    *(The derivative of the inside divided by the inside function itself)*.\n3.  **Derivative of a Square Root:**\n    $$ \\frac{d}{dx} \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \u003d \\frac{1}{2\\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} \\cdot (2x) \u003d \\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} $$\n\n---\n\n### Part 1: The Top Branch (Positive Case)\n**Condition:** $x + \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \u003e 0$\n\nWe need to differentiate:\n$$ \\ln\\left( x + \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \\right) $$\n\nUsing the log rule $\\frac{u\u0027}{u}$:\n*   **The Denominator ($u$):** Stays the same as the inside function:\n    $$ x + \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} $$\n*   **The Numerator ($u\u0027$):** We take the derivative of the inside function:\n    $$ \\frac{d}{dx}\\left( x + \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \\right) \u003d 1 + \\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} $$\n\n**Result:**\n$$ \\frac{1 + \\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}}}{x + \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} $$\n*(This matches the top equation in the image)*.\n\n---\n\n### Part 2: The Bottom Branch (Negative Case)\n**Condition:** $x + \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \u003c 0$\n\nBecause of the absolute value in the original function, when the inside is negative, we negate it. So we differentiate:\n$$ \\ln\\left( -x - \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \\right) $$\n\nUsing the log rule $\\frac{u\u0027}{u}$:\n*   **The Denominator ($u$):** Stays the same as the inside function:\n    $$ -x - \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} $$\n*   **The Numerator ($u\u0027$):** We take the derivative of the inside function:\n    $$ \\frac{d}{dx}\\left( -x - \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} \\right) \u003d -1 - \\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} $$\n\n**Result:**\n$$ \\frac{-1 - \\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}}}{-x - \\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} $$\n*(This matches the bottom equation in the image)*.\n\n### Summary\nThe step simply shows the raw calculation of the derivative $\\frac{u\u0027}{u}$ for both the positive and negative definitions of the absolute value.\n\n*Note: If you were to simplify either of these fractions further, they both simplify to the exact same result:* $\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}}$.",
